questions.text: "She's been working on her listening skills, ___?" (tag)
questions.hint: Positive + present perfect → negative tag "hasn't she"

questions.text: "He didn't use any repair strategies, ___ ___?" (tag)
"We should practise active listening more deliberately, ___?" (modal tag)
"Nobody really practises repair strategies, ___ ___?" (negative word tag)
"I'm getting better at turn-taking, ___?" (I am — special case)
"She barely makes eye contact in presentations, ___ ___?" (negative word "barely")
"___, the key skill is communication repair, not linguistic accuracy." (summarising/getting to the point)
"___, I think we're doing this the wrong way." (gently correcting)
questions.hint: "Actually" = correcting, introducing a contradiction or surprise

questions.text: "___, as I was saying — let's get back to repair strategies." (returning to main point)
questions.hint: "Anyway" = returning to the main point after a digression

questions.text: "A: 'The pause felt very long.' B: '___ ___ — but to the audience it probably seemed normal.'" (accepting a point)
questions.hint: "Fair enough" = accepting a point without necessarily fully agreeing

questions.text: What is "the listener's gap"?
opts: The gap between what speakers say and what they mean
The difference between speech speed and thought speed
The gap in formal education for listening skills
questions.correct: The difference between speech speed and thought speed

questions.text: "It's ___ hard to explain without a concrete example." (hedging: softening)
questions.correct: kind of / sort of / a bit

questions.text: "Let's try that repair strategy again, ___?" (imperative "let's" tag)
questions.hint: "Let's" → "shall we?" = invitation to do something together

questions.text: "___ ___ to practise signposting — it'll make a huge difference." (clarifying what was said)
questions.hint: "I mean" = clarifying or elaborating on what was just said

questions.text: What does research show is the most important predictor of communicative success?
opts: Communication repair — dealing well with breakdowns
questions.correct: Communication repair — dealing well with breakdowns

questions.text: "___ ___ ___, have you practised using minimal responses during conversations?" (off-topic/additional point)
questions.hint: "By the way" = introducing something not directly in the main flow

questions.text: "The issue is pacing — ___ ___ ___, the need to slow down deliberately." (reformulating)
questions.hint: "In other words" = reformulating the same idea more clearly

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses a tag question?
opts: "She is a good listener, doesn't she?"
questions.hint: Modal "can" positive → negative tag "can't he" — correct

questions.text: What does "active listening" involve?
opts: Attending to tone, signalling engagement, and asking clarifying questions
Listening at 2x speed to save time
questions.correct: Attending to tone, signalling engagement, and asking clarifying questions

questions.text: "___ ___ improving pacing, I will record myself speaking and listen back." (with the aim of)
What function does "you know" perform in conversation?
opts: Seeking solidarity or confirmation of mutual understanding
Marking a formal transition between topics
questions.correct: Seeking solidarity or confirmation of mutual understanding
questions.hint: "You know?" = "Do you understand what I mean?" seeking connection

questions.text: The system by which speakers alternate in conversation is called ___.
"She'd benefit from practising in low-stakes settings, ___?"
"Notwithstanding" is a common spoken discourse marker used in conversation.
questions.hint: "Notwithstanding" is a formal written connector — not typically used as a spoken discourse marker

questions.text: What does "communication repair" mean?
opts: Fixing recording equipment in a language lab
The ability to recognise and fix breakdowns in communication
questions.correct: The ability to recognise and fix breakdowns in communication
questions.hint: Listening 3B: "communication repair — recognise breakdown, seek clarification, rephrase"
